name: Beauty Wow
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading. The heading names the
network these frames are cut FOR and the channel is the show they are
cut from, so another show cutting for the same network is one more
folder under it rather than a heading of its own.
Like every channel under this heading it is a frame fetcher rather
than a thumbnail maker: a video goes in and a numbered grid of
vertical stills comes out, each captioned with what was being said
over it.
It is cut to Hall of Femme's design, and that pack is the one to read
first: the frame fetch, the 540x960 vertical output, the
transcription, the rewrite, the card at the foot of the frame, the
palette handed to the user, the highlight that changes FACE and not
colour - all of it is Hall of Femme's and is named here rather than
restated. What makes this show itself is one sentence long: it is set
in Proxima Nova Bold with picked words in Proxima Nova Black, on a
violet-magenta card, in three colours offered for the type and the
same three for the card.
beauty-hacks is the second pack to read, because it is the one that
already made this move - Hall of Femme's design in Proxima Nova - and
everything about the two cuts of that family is argued out there with
the measurements. This pack differs from it in the card and in the
length of the palette, and in nothing else.
beauty-studio is this pack's twin and the two are identical in every
key that reaches the canvas - same faces, same three colours, same
card, same defaults. That is not a duplication to be collapsed into
one folder with two names: they are two shows, commissioned
separately, that happen to have been given the same look, and the next
change asked for on either belongs to that one alone. A shared preset
would quietly make every future change to one a change to both, which
is the opposite of what a channel folder is for. What they genuinely
share - the whole Snapchat caption design - is already a preset.
The id is kebab-case ASCII because it is also the folder name and the
key everything else refers to; the name is the brand.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: Where this show parts company with the packs it was cut from, which
is in the colours and nowhere else. Hall of Femme sets its captions
in Telegraf on a hot pink card; beauty-hacks sets them in Proxima
Nova on a magenta one. This one takes beauty-hacks' type exactly and
puts it on the violet-magenta that pack keeps as a fourth swatch, in
nine pairings of a white, a black and that violet.
Everything else - the size, where the lines break, the capitals, the
freeform text box, the shape of the card, its padding and corners and
shadow, where the block stands on the frame, the drag - is the
Snapchat caption design and is stated once, in
content/presets/snapchat-caption.json. This pack states only what
makes it this show, which is the whole of what a pack under this

_comment_face: Proxima Nova Bold. Which cut that is, why the full name rather
than 'Proxima Nova' is declared, and what the machine may already
know it by are written out in
what capitals at the preset's 40px cost this face, which is
nothing, is written out in beauty-hacks.
The Bold and not the Black, so that a picked word has the heavier
cut to climb into - the argument, and what this pack did before
it, are in beauty-hacks with the measurements.
_comment_color: The channel's own answer, and therefore what every frame is set in
until somebody presses a swatch: a frame stores no colour of its
own until it is given one, and this is what it falls back to (see
state.textColorFor). It is the first of the three in `colors`
below, so the white swatch is the one that shows as chosen on an
untouched frame - though nothing requires that, and the swatch is
found by matching this value rather than by being listed first.
White letters on the violet card is the pairing this show opens
on: the violet is the brand, so it is the CARD - the shape that is
a fifth of the frame and reads before anything on it - and the type
is what has to stay legible against it. White on #BB15D9 is 5.0 to
1, sound for type of any size; black on the same card is 4.2 to 1
and is sound too. Both neutrals clearing 4:1 on the brand colour
is a consequence of that violet sitting near the middle of the
value range rather than at either end of it, and it is what the
pinks and magentas next door cannot offer - beauty-hacks opens at
3.2 and has to argue for it.
_comment_colors: The three colours this show is set in, offered for the letters and
for the card behind them - three buttons each in the title panel
(see editor.renderColorButtons).
The same three in both lists, which is what every pack under this
heading that offers a palette does and for their reason: the point
is the PAIRING. Nine combinations of a white, a black and a
violet-magenta, and the ones worth having are the ones that read.
A palette that could only ever be used one way round would be a
palette of three cards, and this show's look is the pairing rather
than any one of them.
Three rather than the four the packs this was cut from offer,
because the show has one brand colour and not two. Nothing counts
the list - the
panel draws a swatch per entry and the row wraps - so a shorter
palette costs nothing anywhere and a fourth colour, if this show
ever gains one, is one string in this file.
Written in the order the show states its colours in - the two
neutrals, then the brand colour - and the two defaults are picked
out of it by value rather than by position: the type opens on the
first entry and the card on the third. That is the freedom Hall of
Femme's note describes, used here to keep both rows in one order.
Every pairing here reads except the three where a colour is set on
itself, and those are left available for the reason the packs
either side give about white on white - the two lists are
independent because the pairing is the feature, and a rule barring
the three matching combinations would cost the panel more
explaining than an invisible caption costs a user who can see it is
invisible and presses another swatch. A three-colour palette is
where that stops being an argument and starts being obvious: with
nothing but a white, a black and one brand colour, the failures are
exactly the ones anybody would predict.
`text` reaches the highlight as well as the block - see the note
on `colors` in js/channels.js. This channel's highlight is a
different CUT of the face and not a different colour, so what
colour the type is has one answer and not two.
_comment_highlight: A picked word is set in Proxima Nova Black, in the same colour as
the rest of the block: the highlight is WEIGHT, which is Hall of
Femme's highlight and beauty-hacks' both. That the step climbs -
700 to 900, the way Hall of Femme climbs 200 to 800 - and that a
step this short makes a quiet highlight are measured out in
beauty-hacks, which is where that argument belongs and is not
repeated. This pack ran it the other way round until the seven
shows cut to that design were turned together.
The colour it names is the block's, so the recolour draws exactly
what its neighbours are drawn in and the face is the whole of the
difference. Stated all the same, for the fallback reason `color`
above is stated - a highlight that changed colour as well as
No shadow stated, so the preset's null stands: these letters are
on a solid card in a colour the user picked, and the card casts
The mode and the scope come from the preset, which is where the
argument for picking out words rather than lines lives.
_comment_panel: Violet-magenta, and the fill is the one thing about the card this
pack decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow
are the Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
It is the third entry in `colors.panel` above rather than the
first, which is the same freedom `color` uses at the other end of
the row - the swatch that shows as chosen is found by matching
this value and not by being listed first, so both rows can be
written in the order the show states its colours in while the
channel still opens on white type and a violet card.
#BB15D9 is the colour beauty-hacks carries as the fourth swatch in
its palette and never opens on. Here it is the card, which is the
difference between a colour a show can reach and a colour a show
IS - and it is why the two packs read as different brands at a
glance despite sharing every other decision.

_comment_branding: No dark gradient. It exists to hold a title legible against the
photograph, and this title is not against the photograph at all - it
is on a card of its own. A scrim over every still would darken forty
pictures to solve a problem the card has already solved.
